request.spec:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The tree search is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What it does:** there's a new panel with a search box (`search-name`) and a Search button (`search`). Pressing it lists every person on this sheet and the other sheets of its tree whose name or an alias contains the text, ignoring case. Each line (`search-line`) reads `<sheet id> <name> <due-total>`. This sheet's people come first in list order, then the other sheets' people by sheet id. Searching with an empty box lists everyone. The count (`search-count`) clears on each press and only comes back once every sheet has been re-read, so two searches with the same result can still be told apart.

**How it's built:**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree` (`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree.GET.yml` and `RespondWithTree.java`). It returns the other sheets of the tree, sorted by id. It reuses the app's existing tree definition, `People.treeOf`, the same one behind the name-clash rule: a sheet's ancestors and descendants, counting only sheets that exist.
- **Front end:** `src/main/frontend/features/search/search.slot.tsx`. Each person's due-total comes from the same shared calculation the sheet's totals use (`useSheetTotals`), so it matches what their row shows, `n/a` included.

**Behaviour to know about:**
- Retired and held people are always included. The spec only searches after "show retired" has been turned on, so it doesn't settle whether retired people should drop out when it's off.
- If the sheet is being viewed as of a date, the other sheets are shown as of that date too.

No stored data or audit records change: the search only reads.

probe.probe_text:
I read the code and changed nothing. The rules live in the Java backend, mostly in `claim/Figures.java`, `person/Person.java`, `claim/ApplyClaimStatus.java`, `settings/Settings.java` and `rollup/Rollup.java`. The screen works out every figure again itself in TypeScript, mainly in `features/claims/useClaims.ts`, `useSheetTotals.ts` and `rates/useRates.ts`.

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

**Per claim (`claim-row-*`)**
- **amount, date, note, number, status, batch, opened-by, ref, tags, lines, comments, log**: stored values.
  - **number** (`ClaimNumbers.next`) is given when a claim is opened. It is `FY<yyyy>-<n>` by the fiscal year its **due-by** falls in (the count restarts each fiscal year, `fiscalStartMonth` defaults to January, and the sequence is shared across the sheet's tree).
  - Once `periodNumberingFrom` is set and the sheet's today has reached it, the number is `<period>-<n>` instead, or `X-<n>` when the due-by falls in no period.
  - A voided claim keeps its number, and a number is never reused.
- **due-by** (`DueBy.of`): fixed when the claim is added. It is the Nth business day after the claim's date (Saturdays, Sundays and the sheet's holidays are skipped).
  - N is the person's own terms, else their grade's terms on that date, else the sheet's terms on that date (`DEFAULT_TERMS` 14).
  - Later changes to the terms or to the claim's date leave it alone. Adding a holiday (`RefixDueBys`) works it out again for every claim that isn't SETTLED or VOID and is due on or after that holiday.
- **period**: the period that contains the claim's due-by (not its date).
- **due** (`Figures.due`, mirrored by `claimDueCents`):
  - A SETTLED claim shows its frozen `due`.
  - Otherwise its **figure** is used. That is the `statedDue` its person's last statement bound it to (ignored while it is PENDING), else `live` = amount × the rate of the person's grade on the claim's date ÷ 100, rounded to 2 decimals.
  - **Late charge** (`charge`) is added to the figure. For each full 30 days past due-by + grace, it adds the `latePct` in force on that 30-day date, applied to the figure plus the charges so far (it compounds), each step rounded.
  - The result is raised to at least the sheet's `floor` on the claim's date (`DEFAULT_FLOOR` 1.00).
  - With no rate the due is `n/a`. The rate is looked up on this sheet, then up to 3 parent sheets (`Rates.pct`). A rate whose to-date has passed doesn't apply.
  - A **correction** (negative amount) gets neither floor nor charge.
- **rounding / `halfUp`** (`Figures.rounding`): half up when the claim is dated before the sheet's `policyDate`, half to even on or after it. If no policy date is set, the sheet's today is used. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects.
- **overdue**: the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and due-by + `grace` (per grade, in force on the claim's date; 0 if none) is before the sheet's today.
- **deferred**: the sheet's today is before `deferredUntil`. A deferred claim counts in no total, isn't overdue, can't be settled and isn't bound by a statement.
- **stated / statedDue**: set by a statement and cleared by reassigning, splitting or cancelling the statement.
- **late entry**: the claim was added while a soft-closed period contained its due-by.
- **proofs, split-from, locked-by, reminded-on, void reason**: stored values.

**Per person (`person-row-*`)**
- **Which claims count** (`Person.counts`, mirrored by `live`): OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED claims, except:
  - deferred claims;
  - OPEN or PENDING claims dated within one of the person's holds;
  - any OPEN or PENDING claim once today has reached the person's retirement date (`retiredOut`).
  
  A held-out or retired-out claim still counts if a statement binds it and it isn't PENDING.
- **claimed**: the amounts of the counting claims, leaving out corrections.
- **due-total**: the counting claims' dues added up, then capped at the sheet's `cap` in force today.
  - It's `n/a` when no claim has a figure and there's no rate today.
  - **excess** is the amount above the cap.
  - **settled-total** and **open-total** are the same sum before the cap, split into SETTLED and OPEN-or-PENDING claims.
- **overdue-count / overdue-total**: the counting overdue claims and their dues.
- **aged 0–30 / 31–60 / 61+**: dues bucketed by the claim's age, measured from its date to today.
- **cut-total**: the person's share of the pot across pools (`Pools.cuts`).
  - Shares are only used when a pool is balanced (shares add to exactly 100.00) and members are within their dates.
  - Retired or held members get 0.
  - Cuts are rounded half to even; the remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut.
- **period due-totals**: frozen when the period is closed (`PeriodCloser`).
- **Also shown**: grade (the one in force on today; grades are dated), statement count, last stated total and date, holds, retirements, snapshots, aliases, clashing.

**Sheet totals (`rollup-*`, header, summary, months)**
- claimed-total and due-total; n/a people are skipped.
- **The due-total and overdue-total leave out the single highest and lowest person when three or more people have a figure** (`trimmed` / `trimmedTotal`).
- settled and open totals are simply added up.
- Each change audits `ROLLUP` lines, then `TOTALS`, then an `ALERT` when someone's due-total crosses above `alertThreshold`.

**What gets frozen, and when**
- **Settle** freezes `due` at that moment's due.
- **Approve** freezes the live due plus charge, at least the floor.
- **Re-settle** (steward only) freezes it again as an unbound OPEN claim would be today.
- **Statement** (`TakeStatement`) binds every counting claim to its rate figure without charge or floor, and unbinds the rest.
  - It records the total, capped.
  - It can be taken as of a past date (`AsOf`).
  - Cancelling it (steward only) makes the claims live again.
- **Close period** freezes the period's and each person's due-total. Claims count by the status their log shows at the end of the period's last day.
  - **Soft-close** freezes the totals but still allows changes; claims added then are late entries.
  - With `graceDays` set, a today change automatically closes periods whose end + grace has passed.
  - Reopening (steward by default) makes the totals live again.
  - In a **closed** period, claims due-by in it can't be added, edited, opened, settled, voided, reassigned, re-dated, split or locked.

**Who may do what**
- Roles are clerk (the default), steward, and viewer (who can change nothing; `ViewerGuard`). A delegation makes someone steward while it covers today.
- Archived sheets refuse every change.
- The permission matrix (`Settings.allows`) by default: open, settle, void and close for clerk and steward; reassign and reopen for steward.
- **Statuses**:
  - DRAFT can go to OPEN, VOID or DELETED.
  - OPEN can go to SETTLED, PENDING, or VOID.
  - A **clerk** settling a claim whose due is above the `clerkLimit` makes it PENDING instead.
  - Only a steward can approve or reject a PENDING claim, and not the person who opened it or last edited it.
  - The opener or last editor can't settle a claim either.
  - A SETTLED claim can be voided only by a steward, within 7 days of settling.
  - A deleted claim can be restored only on the same sheet-today it was deleted.
- **Other gates**:
  - `proofThreshold` (per grade, else the sheet's) blocks settle or approve when the claim has no proof. This check comes before the clerk-limit one.
  - `noteThreshold` blocks opening a claim without a note.
  - A period `cap` limits OPEN plus PENDING claims per person.
  - When void reasons exist, a void must use one of them.
- **Dates**:
  - Claims are refused when dated after the person's retirement date or inside a past retirement.
  - A deferral must be to a date after today.
  - Re-dating is steward only and keeps the due-by, number and binding.
  - The default claim date is `entryDate`, else today.
- **Bulk actions**:
  - Bulk settle is all or nothing and gets a batch number.
  - Other bulk actions and imports/pastes:
    - Imports and pastes check every line first and refuse the whole lot if any line fails.
    - A people import edits any person matched by name or alias.
    - Bulk open, reassign, re-date, grade and retire act on each item as a single action would, and count the ones refused.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It's moderately hard. The backend is well commented, and `Figures`, `Person.counts` and `ApplyClaimStatus` are close to a single source. But the rules are spread over about 400 one-step files and dozens of `Settings` lookups, and the frontend reimplements the whole calculation (due, charge, rounding, counting, cap, trimming) in parallel. A new developer has to keep two copies in sync, and the comments have already drifted in places: the `useSheetTotals` doc leaves out PENDING, and the `Snapshot` doc doesn't mention grace when describing overdue.
